newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy metalworkers union urges strike over dispute.
newsitem.headline: Italy metalworkers union urges strike over dispute.

text.p: The leader of one of Italy's engineering and metalworkers unions said on Friday he saw no chance of an accord with employers in a bitter six-months pay dispute and pressed for a general strike to support demands.
"A general strike is now necessary and should be prepared politically" as the issue at stake "involves the whole structure of contracts," FIOM secretary-general Claudio Sabattini said.
"Unions have accepted the government's proposal (on a pay increase) to conclude contracts, not to open up whole new negotiations," he told reporters.
FIOM is the largest of the three sector trades unions FIOM, FIM and UILM.

Labour Minister Tiziano Treu is currently in informal contact with unions and the Federmeccanica employers' federation ahead of formal talks which he hopes to resume with both sides next week. The workers' last 2-year contracts expired last June.
In a bid to break the impasse, the government has suggested that workers should be given a 200,000 lire ($130) a month pay rise for the 1996-1998 contract period.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said the government proposals were fair and would not fuel inflation.
The proposals have been welcomed by the unions who has been asking for 230,000 lire a month for their 1.7 million members.
But Federmeccanica, which had offered a pay rise of 139,000 lire, have up to now rejected the government's intervention.
Unions have already held several hours of strikes within the engineering and metalworking sector throughout the country in support of their demands.
Sabattini said," Treu is speaking of a flexible proposal and reckons it is possible to get the two sides together.
"I don't think this is possible. The problem is not only the metalworkers' contract but the whole aspect of the relationship with trades unions in all sectors," he said. $=1,530 lire
